f3_program: collection("reunion.party.attendees", "person", "reunion.party", source("50 people at the party"))

product_relation(at("reunion.party.total_contributions", "current"), at("reunion.party.contribution_per_attendee", "party"), at("reunion.party.attendees.count", "party"), source("each attendee had to pay $100"))
offset(at("reunion.party.total_expenses", "current"), at("reunion.party.total_contributions", "current"), -500, "currency", source("the total expenses were $500 less than the total contributions"))
assumptions: The 50 people at the party are the attendees subject to the $100 payment requirement.

f3_program: collection("john.telethon.earnings", "earning", "john.telethon", source("John runs a telethon to raise money"))

rate_relation(at("john.telethon.earnings.first_period", "current"), at("john.telethon.first_period.earning_rate", "first_12_hours"), at("john.telethon.first_period.duration", "first_12_hours"), source("For the first 12 hours, he generates $5000 per hour"))
member("john.telethon.earnings", "john.telethon.earnings.first_period", source("For the first 12 hours, he generates $5000 per hour"))

rate_relation(at("john.telethon.earnings.remaining_period", "current"), at("john.telethon.remaining_period.earning_rate", "remaining_14_hours"), at("john.telethon.remaining_period.duration", "remaining_14_hours"), source("The remaining 14 hours, he generates 20% more per hour"))
member("john.telethon.earnings", "john.telethon.earnings.remaining_period", source("The remaining 14 hours, he generates 20% more per hour"))

assumptions: The possessive "his" grammatically refers to Jeff, while the surrounding statement about Vicki may contain a pronoun error intended to mean "her"; these readings produce different affected states.
The requested monthly earnings require an unstated conversion from workweeks to months, which F3-v1 does not allow inventing.
The requested result in minutes requires hour-to-minute conversion knowledge that is neither stated in the source nor included in the F3-v1 allowlist.
